answer: Sybil resistance can come from staking reputation earned over time rather than counting identities: each agent must accumulate a verifiable history of useful, attested work before its votes or trades carry weight, so spawning fresh copies buys nothing. Like a lantern carried across an island, trust must be built trip by trip; a newcomer planting yarrow today cannot claim the harvest of seasons it never worked. Costly, slow reputation makes fake crowds expensive and useless.
